Srishti Dasgupta
text:
I’m an architect turned urban planning researcher, currently studying Sustainable Urban Planning and Design at KTH in Stockholm.
I’m interested in resilient cities and the different questions that come with trying to make them more sustainable: how places adapt to climate change, how people move through them, how resources are distributed, and how we make decisions about their future.
This portfolio is a collection of the questions I’ve been exploring along the way.

title: CoolNet Framework
text:
The starting point for CoolNet was urban heat. I wanted to go beyond mapping where temperatures are higher and look at what else is happening in those places, including the infrastructure and environmental resources already present.
Using Malmö as a pilot, I combined heat, vegetation, built form, income, and proximity to water to identify areas where several factors overlap. The framework then explores how existing infrastructure could be used as an asset for adaptation, rather than treating every intervention as something that needs to be newly built.
How can we use what a city already has to make it more resilient to heat?

title: Public Transport For All?
text:
This academic project was an introduction to spatial analysis and spatial econometrics, using Stockholm’s 569 DeSO areas as a case study.
We explored how transit accessibility varies across neighbourhoods and whether these patterns relate to socioeconomic conditions. Starting with exploratory spatial analysis, we compared OLS and spatial regression models to account for spatial dependence in the data.

title: Public Transport For All?
text: This study analyzes transit accessibility across 569 Stockholm DeSO neighborhoods using spatial econometrics to test for socio-economic inequalities.

title: Public Transport For All?
text:
Key Findings

Spatial Disparity: High transit access concentrates in affluent central areas, while low-access pockets appear in northern peripheral zones.
Model Fit: OLS linear regression fails due to spatial autocorrelation (\(R^2 = 0.081\)). The Spatial Error Model (SEM) provides the best overall fit (\(R^2 = 0.355\)).
